_comment: Where an Igbo personal name is BORNE, by region. This is deliberately not provenance: an origin is never the website or compiler a name was collected from. Each row carries the source it rests on. A name absent from this file has no documented regional concentration, and its entry shows no Origin. Vocabulary and validation live in packages/core/src/regions.ts and packages/db/src/import/name-regions.ts.
_researchNotes:
WHAT THIS FILE IS
=================
Every entry in "regions" is an Igbo personal name for which a source that was actually fetched,
read and quoted states either (a) that the name is used in / characteristic of / peculiar to a
particular Igbo region or sub-group, or (b) that the name belongs to a documented set of names
collected from that place. No name was assigned a region because it "sounds like" it belongs
there, and no name was assigned a region on the strength of a single bearer from that region.

"name" is written in Standard Igbo spelling, one word, capitalised, WITHOUT tone marks or dotted
vowels (ị ọ ụ are written i o u). This was a deliberate normalisation so the field is a stable
dictionary key; the cited sources carry the full diacritics. Where a source attests only a
dialect-variety form of a name (an Etche, Ikwerre, Ogba, Ekpeye, Igbuzo/Enuani, Abakaliki or Ika
form), that variety form is recorded as given, with the variety named in "origins".

GENERAL / PAN-IGBO NAMES STAY OUT (rule 4)
==========================================
Many of the regional corpora below also contain ordinary Igboland-wide names. Those were dropped
on purpose, e.g. Obinna, Chinedu, Chukwuemeka, Chukwuma, Ozioma, Okoro, Nnamdi, Obi, Udo, Nwosu,
Nwankwo, Nweke, Nwoye, Ndubuisi, Ugochukwu, Nwaamaka. The Awka study of 145 dying names itself
makes this point, saying modern Chukwu- names "are not dialect specific ... you cannot tell the
region of origin". So regional coverage is thinner than the raw corpora would suggest, and that
is intentional.
Leaving a name out is also the answer whenever two credible sources put the same name in
different places, UNLESS both attributions are listed in "origins".

COVERED — and how strong the evidence is
========================================
Strong (peer-reviewed or scholarly corpora with an explicit regional claim):
  Nsukka   (81)  Agbo, Opata & Okwueze (2022), HTS Teologiese Studies 78(3) a6977: five tables
                 of "Nsukka Ugwu personal names", with the source asserting Ugwu names occur
                 among Nsukka people "more than any other Igbo group". Plus Okpoko (2025),
                 Nigerian Journal of African Studies 7(3), a 20-name Nsukka corpus.
  Enuani   (161) Oweleke (2021), ACAL50 ch.13 - 300 names gathered from the Igbuzo-Igbo
                 community (Igbuzo = Ibusa, Delta State), tables headed "Igbuzo-Igbo Names", and
                 the explicit statement that ashi names "are prevalent in the Enuani-Igbo
                 cosmology". Plus a community compendium of 73 Ibusa FAMILY names that the author
                 documents as "completely unique to Ibusa" - note these are surnames, not given
                 names.
  Etche    (102) Nwala (2018), Global Journal of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences 6(10),
                 "A New Dawn in Etche Names": 103 Etche personal names tabulated by category.
  Awka     (125) Udoye, "The Semantics of Oka Dying Anthroponyms" (Onoma/Debrecen volume): 145
                 names collected by interview from elderly Oka (Awka) farmers; plus Udoye &
                 Ofoegbu (2011) on Awka theocentric names.
  Afikpo   (79)  Emeka-Nwobia (2016), Research on Humanities and Social Sciences 6(12): a
                 "Glossary of some Afikpo Names" introduced as "names peculiar to Afikpo-Igbo
                 cultural group".
  Ogba     (73)  Ohia (2025), Icheke Journal, on Ogba women's names and sobriquets; plus the
                 Ogba Language Committee's Ogba-English dictionary (Kay Williamson papers,
                 archive.org), whose entries are explicitly glossed as personal names.
  Onitsha  (87)  Two independent morpho-syntactic studies of 250 Onitsha personal names sampled
                 from Onitsha school lists and Onitsha religious associations (nigerianjournals
                 online NJAH 5(4); JLTR/academypublication).
  Abakaliki(35)  Ozo, Emeka-Nwobia & Obinna, EBSU Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities:
                 five tables of nwa- names collected solely from Abakaliki informants, each with
                 its Abakaliki place/market/deity referent spelled out.
  Ekpeye   (93)  A community language-initiative page ("Ekpeye names are usually given to Ekpeye
                 children") and an Ekpeye-community news page headed "EKPEYE NAMES AND MEANING".
                 Weaker genre, but both state the names belong to Ekpeye of Ahoada, Rivers State.
  Imo/Abia/Anambra/Enugu (37/33/29 via state+sub-group)  Obiorah (2021), SGOJAHDS 4(1): 600
                 names from university registers that record each bearer's STATE OF ORIGIN, giving
                 region-to-sound-variant data (/h/ vs /r/, /h/ vs /f~v/, /l/ vs /n/, /r/ vs /l/).
                 This is the single best source in the file for the "same name, different regional
                 form" problem, and it is why e.g. Obioha is Imo+Abia while Obiora is
                 Anambra+Enugu.
  Ikwerre+Etche (11) Idika & Iwuchukwu (2018), JOLAN 21(1), Example 2 "Some names peculiar to
                 regional dialects of Igbo-land": this is the only source found that makes a
                 per-dialect peculiarity claim for Abia, Anambra, Delta, Ebonyi, Enugu, Imo and
                 the "Rivers (Ikwere/Etche Axis)". For the Rivers items the source does not
                 separate Ikwerre from Etche, so both are recorded rather than one being picked.
  Ika      (22)  A community web compilation headed "900+ IKA NAMES AND THEIR MEANINGS (A-Z)".
                 Non-academic and unverified as to provenance - treat as LOW CONFIDENCE.
  Ukwuani  (7)   Ehie Journal (University of Delta, Agbor) on Ndokwa Ukwuani women's names.
  Anioma   (15)  Oweleke (2021) names tied to Oboshi, "a river deity in Igbuzo"; the JOLAN Delta
                 list; and Odimbu/Olisemenke, documented as Enuani names borne in Ibusa, Asaba and
                 Okpanam.
  Ikwerre  (21)  One IJAH paper on Anglican intercultural communication among the Ikwerre that
                 names Ikwerre personal names (Nwekhne, Chinugonum, Woroma, Nnedah, Enyidah,
                 Azundah, Chimzi, Chitukpobi); one paper on Ikwerre/Etche wife-renaming that
                 contrasts "OvuNziyaa (Ikwerre)" with "Ugo Diyaa (Etche)"; one Ikwerre-language
                 thesis naming Amadi/Wali. Ikwerre has NO dedicated onomastic study in the open
                 literature, so this is the weakest of the well-covered groups.
  Afikpo/Ezza/Ebonyi:  7 names from the JOLAN Ebonyi dialect list; Ezza rests on a single
                 indirect case (Nwezza = Nwa + Ezza inside the Abakaliki dataset).

WHERE THE PAIR "Nnewi + Enugu" COMES FROM
=========================================
Azuka Onwuka's Nnewi account documents that Nnewi people ABANDONED their /h/ and /l/ name forms
for the prestige /r/ forms used elsewhere (Ohamadike -> Oramadike, Obioha -> Obiora,
Ebele -> Ebere, Chinyelu -> Chinyere). Only the retained indigenous Nnewi forms (Iloka, Ileka,
Ilechukwu, Iloegbu, Iloegbunam, Ajuluchukwu, Obiajulu, Nnoli, ...) are recorded here as Nnewi.
Where a name is genuinely attested for both an /h/ area and Nnewi, both origins are listed.

WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED — these regions have ZERO names in this file
==========================================================================
  Aro (Arochukwu)   six searches; nothing in the reachable literature documents a set of Aro
                    personal names. General Aro history and the Aro Confederacy are well
                    covered, personal names are not.
  Ndoki             one lead only ("the name Ubani is common among the Ndoki") but it sits in a
                    passage about Bonny/Opobo and toponymy, so it was rejected rather than
                    guessed. Ubani is recorded under Ngwa instead, where a paper lists it
                    explicitly as a Ngwa anthroponym.
  Ohaji, Mbaise, Orlu, Owerri, Okigwe   no documented personal-name corpus found. Searches on
                    these turned up Mbaise/Ohaji COMMUNITY (place) names, dialect-phonology
                    papers, and pan-Igbo name lists - none of which is a personal-name set.
                    Note that the Mbaise place-name paper states the forenames behind those
                    villages are ordinary Igbo names; its examples (Umuagụ, Umueze) are not
                    personal names in use.
  Ikwo              nothing. Wiki/migration sources only.
  Anambra-wide / Imo-wide / Abia-wide / Ebonyi-wide / Enugu-wide as STATE labels exist only
                    where the source itself stopped at the state (JOLAN dialect list, Obiorah
                    register data).

DEAD ENDS AND BLOCKED SOURCES (searches or fetches that produced nothing usable)
================================================================================
- zenodo.org (403 "unusual traffic" from this network): the ACAL50 chapter had to be read from
  a Wayback Machine snapshot. ajol.info (AWS WAF challenge), sciencedirect, researchgate,
  academia.edu, nairaland, core.ac.uk download links, iiste.org and paperity all blocked or
  returned empty bodies; where possible the same text was reached through a mirror or the CORE
  reader page.
- General Igbo onomastics sources that turned out to be regionally empty and were therefore NOT
  used for attribution: Nkamigbo (2019) "The Sociolinguistics of Igbo Personal Names";
  Okwuchukwu (2025) on Chi/Chukwu names from UNIZIK Awka class lists (explicitly a mixed-region
  student corpus); Onumajuru (2016); Ogbulogo (1999); Idika & Iwuchukwu's own pet-name data;
  the JOLAN/NJAS/NJAH orthography-of-Igbo-names papers (toponyms only); Igbo Studies Review
  no. 9 wealth-based names (pan-Igbo); Mbaise "Abigbo" folklore papers; Ukwuani folklore and
  proverbs; the Etche/Ikwerre wife-renaming paper's theory sections.
- An Ekpeye source at bochnewsng.com initially 404'd; the live URL has "meanings" (plural) and
  was verified (all 22 names present on the page).
- Roughly 20 further sources read by the region researchers were real onomastics papers about a
  different region than the one they were chasing; they are listed in
  names-region-work/findings/*.json under "sources_read".

HOW MANY SOURCES WERE READ
==========================
About 70 sources were fetched and read across this task (academic papers, journal issues,
dissentations, dictionaries, community/cultural pages). The mechanically re-checked ones are in
names-region-work/findings/*.json and names-region-work/verified/*.json. Verification performed
on the subagent findings: rivers 258/258 names+quotes matched their source text; imo 27 Obiorah
entries were corrected from "Imo" to "Imo + Abia" because the source says both; abia-anambra
136/140 Awka names matched verbatim (the other 4 come from the second Awka paper) and 23/23 Nnewi
matched; anioma 22/22 Ika and 73/73 Ibusa names matched after diacritic normalisation; ebonyi
accepted on the strength of its quotes against the Abakaliki and Afikpo papers.

CAVEATS ON SPELLING
===================
Some corpora have noisy spelling. The Ogba dictionary is a provisional, never-corrected
circulation version (its own foreword says so) and uses Ogba post-nasalised consonants (Cn), so
forms such as Aznudimma, Iznido and Ugbnani are Ogba orthography, not typos. The Ogba sobriquet
paper and the Etche paper contain a few evident typos in the printed names. Names whose exact
spelling is uncertain should be re-checked against the printed sources before publication.

ENTRY COUNTS
============
1000 names in total. By origin (a name with two documented origins is counted in each):
Abakaliki 35, Abia 37, Afikpo 79, Anambra 37, Anioma 16,
Awka 124, Ebonyi 8, Ekpeye 93, Enuani 161, Enugu 30,
Etche 91, Ezza 1, Ika 22, Ikwerre 20, Imo 35,
Ngwa 19, Nnewi 23, Nsukka 81, Ogba 73, Onitsha 86,
Ukwuani 7.
Zero: Ohaji, Ndoki, Aro, Mbaise, Orlu, Owerri, Okigwe, Ikwo.
71 names carry more than one documented origin; those are the names two independent sources
placed in different (or jointly named) regions, listed rather than arbitrarily reduced to one.
Where one source gives a state and another gives a sub-group of that state, BOTH are kept
(e.g. Azikiwe = Anambra + Onitsha, Ugwuanyi = Enugu + Nsukka): the task says to prefer a
documented sub-group, but it also says to list every documented origin, and keeping both avoids
asserting a narrower region than a source supports.

ONE FLAGGED ENTRY
=================
"Ogbuide" (Imo) is the single entry whose source text could not be re-fetched by the lead
agent: the Genealogy (MDPI) article is Cloudflare-blocked from this network. Its DOI
(https://doi.org/10.3390/genealogy10030100) was confirmed against Crossref as
Kamalu, Ugochukwu & Ogamba, "Anthropological Linguistic Study of Names as Representations of
Family and Community Origins and Identity Among the Igbo of Southeastern Nigeria". The claim
is flagged in the entry's own note field.


A LEAD WORTH BUYING
===================
"Ikwere" is the weakest well-covered group (20 names) because no Ikwerre onomastic study exists in
the open literature. The single richest Ikwerre source is a PRINT book with no readable text
online: "Rewhna IWHURUOHNA: 2,000 Ikwerre Native Names and their Meanings" (ISBN 9789785512144).
If a copy can be obtained, Ikwerre could be brought up to the level of its neighbours. For the
same reason no Ikwerre-vs-Etche discrimination exists except one sentence in Onyeso, Eze & Okeh
(2026) contrasting "OvuNziyaa (Ikwerre)" with "Ugo Diyaa (Etche)".

NAMES EXPLICITLY REJECTED AS PAN-IGBO
=====================================
Beyond the list given above, names that sat inside a regional list but were dropped because both
the region researcher and the lead agent judged them Igboland-wide: Umunnakwe, Onwukwe, Nnochiri,
Nwaorie, Nwafo, Nwala, Nwancha, Azunna, Azuonwu, Nwanyanwu, Amadi, Dike, Ezeji, Nnenna, Umuada,
Okechukwu, Ndidi, plus every Chi-/Chukwu- theophoric name in the Etche and Mba-clan Etche lists.
Also rejected as ambiguous (the sentence groups them with place names, so it is unclear whether
they are personal names at all): Ovundah and Yelemaekhile from the Rumu/Umu discussion.

OGBA SOBRIQUETS
===============
25 of the Ogba entries come from Ohia (2025) on Ogba women's sobriquets. These are aliases taken
at marriage or in adulthood, NOT birth names; every such entry says so in its own note.
